_readme: Settings for the screen_ai plugin: screenshot understanding, auto-reply and error fixing.
Everything that sends a message you did not type yourself is off until you turn it on.
The fast path: fill in 'contacts', then arm with mode 'draft' to review drafts, or
mode 'send' for unattended replies. Nothing is ever sent to a contact whose entry is
After editing this file the plugin picks the changes up on the next look — no restart.

capture._note: reuse_seconds avoids taking three screenshots of a screen that has not moved.

_note: Models are tried in the order below, but the client re-orders them by what has
actually been working: a model that has answered quickly before goes first, a model
that returned 404 is remembered as retired and skipped for good, one that returned 503
cools off for 90s, and a model that has never been tried still gets its turn in this
configured order.
Measured on this machine, four INTERLEAVED trials per model with these settings:
gemini-3.6-flash answered every time (2.40s median on short text, 4.31s median on
a real screenshot); gemini-3.1-flash-lite managed 1 of 4 text calls and averaged
9.11s on images. A single sample had suggested the opposite — alternating trials
settled it. gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.7-flash, gemini-3.5-flash and
gemini-flash-latest all returned 503, and
gemini-3.5-flash-lite / gemini-flash-lite-latest answered but took 32s and 55s.
2.5-generation names return 404. So the fastest verified models come first, the
newest (best quality, often throttled) follow, and the measured-slow ones sit at
the back. `max_seconds_per_call` caps the whole walk, so a burst of slow failures
can never turn one look into a two-minute wait.
Enforced in code before an image is sent, not requested in a prompt.
blocked_apps is matched case-insensitively against the app name, window title and
the first few strings of visible text. redact_regions paints rectangles black on the
frame itself, so those pixels never leave the machine.
auto_send false = drafts are written and queued for your approval, never sent.
arm(confirm=true, mode='send') turns unattended sending on for the session.
block_risky_drafts stops anything that promises, agrees to plans, states a time, or
touches money or credentials — those are held for you regardless of mode.
The background loop only runs while armed. It is idempotent: arming twice does
nothing extra. A frame identical to the previous one is skipped without a model call,
which is what keeps a long-running watch cheap.
_safety_note: resume_after_restart: false — a watch armed once used to come back on every launch and
photograph the screen in the background. It must now be armed deliberately, in the
max_captures_per_hour: 24 — hard ceiling; the watch stops itself and says so.
pause_while_user_talking_seconds: 20 — a watch tick never steals the look the user's own
request is using, and never fires while they are mid-sentence.
